pyflip.instruments package¶

Submodules¶

pyflip.instruments.JWSTNIRCamData module¶

pyflip.instruments.JWSTNIRCamData.assemble_JWST_NIRCam_coron(data_dir, num_det_px, psf_pixel_scale=0.062424185, diameter=6.603464, DEVICE='cuda')[source]¶

Assemble a FLIP NIRCam coron model, given some model parameters. Again, quite hard coded: - data_dir must be where the data is, and the folder structure must follow what ‘generate_STPSF_model_params’ generates.

This argument must be the same as folder_to_save in the function above.

  • psf_pixel_scale: Must match the STPSF model: 0.062424185 if channel == ‘long’; half of that if ‘short’.

    TODO: Clean this up to get pixel scale automtically from STPSF insturment, maybe with a wrapper

pyflip.instruments.JWSTNIRCamData.create_STPSF_model(from_obs=None, instrument='NIRCam', inst_params={'bar_offset': 'narrow', 'filter': 'F444W', 'image_mask': 'MASK335R', 'pupil_mask': 'CIRCLYOT'}, obs_time='2022-07-29T23:00:00', choice='closest')[source]¶

Create a STPSF instrument given a combination of filters and such. Mostly a small convenience function to apply Kellen’s pupil shear.

If ‘from_obs’ is used, it will use STPSF’s automatic generator from a FITS file for an observation. Otherwise, parameters must be plugged in manually.

Examples of valid/realistic parameter combinations: - Filter = any, image_mask = ‘MASK335R’, pupil_mask = ‘CIRCLYOT’ (for most typical round coronagraph obs) - Filter = any, image_mask = ‘MASKLWB’, pupil_mask = ‘WEDGELYOT’, bar_offset = ‘narrow’ (for bar coronagraphy in the NARROW fiducial point override)

pyflip.instruments.JWSTNIRCamData.generate_STPSF_model_params(stpsf_instrument, spec_type='A1V', catalog_spec='phoenix', input_spectrum=None, num_wl=21, oversample=2, folder_to_save='mydata', return_data=False)[source]¶

Take a STPSF instrument and create FLIP-friendly model parameters.

TODO: Now it is pretty hard coded to the NIRCam coronagraphs/the things we care about; in the future we might want to make this more flexible to turn any STPSF model automatically into FLIP format.

In its current form, this saves the following instrument parameters formatted for FLIP: - The JWST primary mirror transmission - The JWST primary mirror OPD - The image plane focal plane mask PER WAVELENGTH, because currently we follow STPSF, and each wavelength results

in a different pixel scale when FFT’d into the image plane. It also has the indicated oversampling (we typically use 2048 pixels).

  • The Lyot stop transmission

  • The combined NIRCam OPD PER WAVELENGTH, because it has chromatic components.

    This is the COMBINED OPD effect, and it incorporates the OPD at of the NIRCam coronagraph itself at this field point, wavelength-dependent defocus, and wavelength-dependent OPD from the coronagraph wedge. In the future these could be separated if we want to isolate them; currently we combine them (following STPSF)

As a rule of thumb, we typically use 21 wavelengths for wide filters and 9 wavelengths for medium filters, but this has not been rigorously optimized.

pyflip.instruments.JWSTNIRCamData.load_and_crop_obs(filepath, num_det_px=80, coron_type='MASK335R', crop_params=None)[source]¶

Utility function to load JWST data as FITS files and format them for FLIP.

Current automatic options are ‘MASK335R’ and ‘MASKLWB_NARROW’.
